metadata.title: Ambraseys (2002) Figure 1 study-area boundaries -- Region A (Marmara Sea region) and Region B (Marmara Basin)
metadata.source_full: Ambraseys, N. (2002), The Seismic Activity of the Marmara Sea Region over the Last 2000 Years, Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America, 92(1), 1-18
metadata.figure: Figure 1 (location map, inset showing study areas A and B), p.2
metadata.purpose: These two rectangles are the paper's own nested study-area definitions, digitized for transparency/context alongside data/marmara_historical_ambraseys_2002.json (the 55-event Table 1 catalog) and data/marmara_ambraseys_eq_historical_crosswalk.json. They are NOT earthquake data -- they represent the geographic extent the paper's analysis is scoped to.
metadata.region_distinction: Region A ('Marmara Sea region') is the paper's full study area and corresponds to the geographic scope of the 55-event Table 1 catalog (all catalog events fall within/near Region A). Region B ('Marmara Basin') is explicitly a SMALLER, nested sub-area (~4x smaller by area, 'half as long and half as wide' per the source text) used specifically for the seismic-moment-release-rate analysis (Figures 9, 11, 13) and the shear-velocity comparison (Table 3) -- it is NOT the area the 55-event catalog was selected from, and should not be presented as such.
metadata.coordinate_status: figure-derived, not explicitly stated in text -- the source text gives only relative/qualitative descriptions of Region B ('4 times smaller', 'half as long and half as wide', '210-km-long'), no numeric lat/lon for either region. Coordinates below were obtained by calibrating the figure's own axis tick marks (24/28/32 deg longitude at top, 42/38 deg latitude at right) via pixel-position detection, then reading the four dashed-rectangle edges for each region against that calibration.
metadata.coordinate_validation: independently reproduced by two distinct pixel-based measurement methods (row/column ink-density peak detection, and connected-component dash-cluster detection with outlier rejection); differences between the two methods were <0.02 degrees on every edge of both rectangles. Values below are the average of the two methods.
metadata.calibration_reference: x0=1494px/lon0=24.0E/sx=432.8px per degree; y0=1774px/lat0=42.0N/sy=620.25px per degree (calibrated against the raw embedded page-1 figure image, 6150x6507px, extracted from the user's own Zotero PDF copy)
known_limitations: Both regions are simple axis-aligned rectangles as drawn in the source figure -- no attempt was made to infer a more complex boundary; the paper itself draws them as plain dashed boxes.
Edge precision is estimated at roughly +/-0.02 degrees (~1-2 km) based on the two-method cross-validation; this is a hand-drawn inset map in a location-reference figure, not a precision GIS boundary.

Region B should not be interpreted as 'the area the 55-event catalog covers' -- that is Region A. Region B is a narrower analytical sub-area used only for specific moment-release and shear-velocity calculations discussed in the paper.
metadata.digitized_by: Claude (calibrated pixel tracing from the user's Zotero PDF copy of Figure 1), 2026-09-13
